Katalog Berita (Halaman 45/57)

#2462. Talking to Icarus Football, the kit designers adding beauty to the game

“Football shirts give off a lot of signals,” Robby Smukler says. “They can indicate what you’re passionate about, where you’re from, and even your politics in some cases. That’s part of what makes them so special as a piece of clothing—there’s really so much that’s tied into a football shirt.”

It’s easy to agree with that sentiment. Combining place, philosophy, art, design, and, for some, religion and a sense of belonging, football shirts are the acceptable fashion piece that allow anyone to make a splash and stand out from the crowd. Whether worn at a match, at a festival, or for a quick trip to the coffee house, jerseys are the accessible statement piece anyone can pull off (or on) with ease.

You might also say that they’re a great way of telling your nosey Red neighbour that you’re a die-hard Blue in that silent “fuck you” kind of way.

Robby is the founder of Icarus Football, a custom kit design service making tailor-made shirts for everyone, from five-a-side teams to semi-pro outfits. Quintessentially one-of-a-kind, their jerseys offer one-off pieces that faithfully highlight the sui generis of each club.

Robby’s dream of being a creative started many years ago when he became fascinated with sketching football-themed creations at an early age. As a child growing up in Philadelphia, he would read up on cities and countries near and far before making jersey and crest designs to pass the time.

From the get-go, imagination and flair were key parts of his approach, and that has continued to this day, allowing him to realize all sorts of concepts for teams from a myriad of backgrounds. “We design shirts with fans of a club in mind rather than players. And fans are increasingly looking for creative designs to wear, whether that be for pick-up games in the park or music festivals.

“I think part of the appeal comes from the colours and designs used on football kits. They’re often a lot more creative and out-there than traditional men’s clothing, so football shirts offer something different. They’re also comfortable, so they fit in with the growing trend towards athleisure,” Robby explains.

Indeed, football jerseys are very in today; whether it’s the new releases by the top clubs or the retro classic continually making a comeback, there is a lot of demand for eye-catching sportswear.

Icarus Football’s jerseys appeal to a wide audience because they are steeped in personality, unique designs, and more. As Robby explains, the shirts they make are inspired by each club’s “history, iconography, imagery, fan culture, location”, offering an antidote to the bland factory-manufactured shirts that clubs and fans are often forced to buy.

Robby and his team offer distinctive, eye-catching shirts that clubs can wear with pride when they take to the field. Fans, too, can appreciate the carnival of colour that defines many of their creations, the tailored detail of the pieces, and the thoughtful artistry, too.

“For us, a design that references a team’s culture and history makes a shirt special. But for it to be totally iconic–it needs to be worn in an interesting context.

“The Holland ’88 and Germany ’90 jerseys are two of the most iconic designs of all time, and deservedly so. They’re amazing designs. But if they weren’t worn by those trophy-winning teams and wrapped up in those historic moments, I don’t think they would be considered as legendary as they are.

“The moments in which shirts are worn and the players that wear them both contribute to the status of a shirt. That also speaks a little bit as to why retro shirts have become so popular.

“Legendary players from the 80s/90s seem cooler, perhaps because a lot of young people didn’t get to watch them play during their careers. Only getting to watch legends like [Gheorge] Hagi, [Marco] Van Basten, [Johan] Cruyff, [Michael] Laudrup, [Roberto] Baggio …through limited YouTube videos and highlight reels makes them appear all the more legendary. And that rubs off a bit on the status of the shirts that they wore.”

Robbie’s thoughts confirm the notion that retro jerseys have long been on the comeback trail.

Instagram is full of posts with throwbacks to iconic shirts of old – and to football’s traditions and magical teams. Boca Juniors, Fiorentina, Liverpool, AC Milan, Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona, and more are just some of the clubs that feature heavily in posts dripping with charm, style, and those-were-the-days vibes.

After all, what football fan can scroll past a post of Diego Maradona in the pomp of his career wearing that special Mars-sponsored Napoli shirt without leaving an emphatic ‘like’?

Nostalgia is a big art of the apparent resurgence in popularity of retro replicas, but kit designer Robbie also believes retro shirts are popular because of something else, too “Retro shirts are baggier and made from materials that are almost closer to modern-day sweatshirts than football shirts. That plays well when it comes to fashion.”

Indeed, Icarus Football’s line of historical concept jerseys speaks to how sought-after retro-style kits are. “We really love working on our historical jersey range. We love history, and these jerseys are playful attempts at football shirts for bygone civilizations (e.g., Ancient Egypt, Mesopotamia, The Republic of Venice, The Mongol Empire). There’s so much content to use as inspiration for these designs.”

New Amsterdam FC and Louisiana Krewe are two clubs Icarus FC have worked with in recent times, and they have also worked with clubs in the Ghana Premier League, among so many others. For several years, they have provided a nonconformist approach to fashioning beautiful jerseys shining with distinction. So, what about the future – what teams would Robby and his crew like to work with?

“At a top, top level, it would have to be a national team that’s open to something creative and experimental. National sides have so much imagery, history, and iconography that can be used for the purposes of a personal design. As a geography nerd, I’m extremely interested in working with national sides off the beaten path.

“I’d get just as much joy out of creating a design for Belize as for Brazil. Same thing goes for clubs. Give me TP Mazembe in the Congo, FC Noah in Armenia, and FC Ulaanbaatar in Mongolia (just to name a few) and I’d be a happy man.”

#2461. Former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin on Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy saga: 'It's a dumpster fire'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Pittsburgh Steelers are facing a unique kind of adversity as they prepare for their "Black Friday" matchup against the Denver Broncos. Late Tuesday night, the team announced it was benching future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers in favor of Mason Rudolph. On Wednesday, Rodgers appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show" and lashed out against Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy. That led to his release.

Rodgers' attack of his head coach felt personal and unprecedented. On national television, he accused McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings, not putting in the work required to prepare for upcoming opponents, and failing to connect with players in his first season as the lead man in Pittsburgh. The breaking point, according to Rodgers, was when McCarthy, 63, broke down the team saying, "1-2-3 Packers!" at halftime of Sunday's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. McCarthy last coached the Packers in 2018. The coach admitted using the wrong team name during a press conference on Wednesday.

Fans and former players have not been shy in voicing their opinions on this wild saga, but one man we all wanted to hear from about this situation was Mike Tomlin. The new NBC analyst spent 19 years as the head coach of the Steelers, winning Super Bowl XLIII with the franchise in 2009. He famously never registered a losing season with the Steelers, and coached Rodgers during his final year as coach in 2025. During halftime of the Kansas City Chiefs at Buffalo Bills matchup on Thanksgiving, he revealed what he thought about Rodgers' actions in an interview with Mike Tirico.

Tomlin said he had a range of emotions hearing what Rodgers had to say about his new head coach, but the prevailing emotion was "general sadness."

"Sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career in the quarterback Aaron Rodgers, and just at the macro level whether it's organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum," Tomlin said. "Those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football."

Did it shock Tomlin that Rodgers went this route?

"It certainly did," Tomlin said. "Particularly because I know both men involved. [I] certainly had a lot of intimate work and development of relationships with Aaron over the last couple of years and have known and competed with Mike and respected and appreciated him as a coach for a long time."

Tomlin was asked how Rodgers was viewed in the locker room during his one year in Pittsburgh.

"He was beloved, and I'm not over-exaggerating that," Tomlin said. "He worked at it, and people appreciated his openness to getting to know and understand the Steeler culture. To be engaged with teammates, and particularly from my perspective, I worked with a lot of veteran players over the years and at times they lose a little patience for the process or they lose patience for relationships with younger guys, etcetera. Man, he seemed to embrace all of that and really embrace it in a real natural way."

Tomlin was asked whether McCarthy can effectively lead this team for the rest of the season?

"You know it certainly created some challenges and 'challenges' is probably an understatement if all of those things are true. Certainly, the '1-2-3 Packers' is because he acknowledged that. But his ability to overcome that or inability to overcome that in my opinion is based on relationships, and the depth of those relationships and how those guys feel about him or how those guys buy into what he's selling. And so certainly he's been there a short period of time, and so it makes you wonder the level of that challenge. But it will be relationship-based, his ability to overcome the things that you mentioned."

Tirico asked Tomlin what his emotions were being a coach that was involved with the Steelers franchise for nearly two decades

"I'm upset about it, it's a dumpster fire," Tomlin said. "And I don't say that in a judgemental way; I've presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years. But it certainly is upsetting, and I'm sure Steeler Nation is upset."

There were plenty of bewildering aspects of this story. Tom Pelissero reported that frustration had been building behind the scenes among some players and coaches about Rodgers, who was calling plays himself. The quarterback reportedly went to McCarthy and demanded more changes related to the play-calling process. The coach received feedback from players and coaches indicating that's not what they wanted. Rodgers then issued an ultimatum: "Run things my way, or I quit."

ESPN's Brooke Pryor also reported that "multiple league sources corroborated Rodgers' account" during his appearance on ESPN. According to Pryor, "One source texted: 'It's all true.'" Anonymous team sources acknowledged Rodgers' claim that McCarthy fell asleep in meetings, according to The Athletic.

With that said, Rodgers did violate "the sanctity of the NFL locker room," as Tom Brady mentioned during his broadcast of the Thanksgiving matchup between the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys. One of the best quarterbacks in NFL history dropped a grenade in his building and walked away.

“Nobody wins when the family feuds.”@TomBrady on Aaron Rodgers pic.twitter.com/qLtmKL5oif

The Steelers locker room was expectedly mum on the situation, but quarterback Drew Allar did say it was "kinda sad to see," because of the respect he has for Rodgers.

There were plenty of others that did not hold their tongues, however. Former Packers offensive lineman T.J. Lang alleged Rodgers was a hypocrite for blacklisting players for telling the truth at other times, then going scorched-earth this week. Lang even said he's in a group chat with "a whole lot of former teammates" that feel the exact same way that he does.

"I think it's despicable," Lang said on 97.1 The Ticket in Detroit. "I think that Aaron Rodgers just became everything that he has bitched about and moaned about over the last 10 years with former coaches, former teammates airing grievances out, giving opinions out in the media. He has blacklisted, I don't know how many former teammates from just simple comments telling the truth because he just he was sick of it."

TJ Lang on his former teammate Aaron Rodgers pic.twitter.com/0oiS3PybCn

Former Packers receiver and teammate James Jones said something very similar.

"How do you jump on Pat McAfee's show and say all this? Come on, man," Jones said on the Speakeasy podcast. "My text thread is full of texts and group chats with a lot of my teammates right now, and none are on 12's side, especially the ones that know Mike."

Another former Packers wideout in Greg Jennings chimed in on "First Things First," saying he was surprised by a lot of Rodgers' comments, and called his decision to air out this dirty laundry "distasteful."

"If you truly cared about more than just yourself, then you don't do this to everybody in that locker room that you just called brothers," Jennings said. "They are playing for something. You are no longer playing for anything."

@GregJennings weighs in on Steelers releasing former teammate Aaron Rodgers:“It was very distasteful… If you truly cared about more than just yourself, then you don’t do this to everybody in that locker room that you just called brothers... They are playing for something.” pic.twitter.com/whPyBO7K2p

Steelers president Art Rooney II released a statement on Thursday saying he stands behind McCarthy despite Rodgers' criticisms.

"I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he'll be our coach this season, next season and beyond," Rooney told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. "The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can't be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can't live with that."

#2460. Sons of LeBron James, Carmelo Anthony among notable college basketball players with family ties to NBA

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

One of the best parts about Thanksgiving is reuniting with family, eating good food and watching sports. Whether it's watching a massive NFC North showdown on CBS between the Lions and Bears or tuning into one of the best college basketball games of the week between No. 11 Michigan State and Arkansas, Thanksgiving will have something for everybody.

Michigan State star Jeremy Fears Jr. was named Preseason Player of the Year by CBS Sports and has looked the part through the first three weeks of the season. Fears, who is the No. 35 ranked player on CBS Sports Prospect Rankings for the 2027 NBA Draft, is also improving his draft stock ahead of a wide-open draft with his play.

If Fears is drafted in the first round this summer, he will join exclusive company with his brother Jeremiah Fears, who was selected No. 8 overall by the Pelicans in 2025. The Fears brothers could become the latest siblings to both get drafted in the first round of the NBA Draft if Jeremy is selected on the first day.

Here is a list of siblings who were both drafted in the first round of the NBA Draft.

Fears isn't the only notable sibling playing college basketball this season. Bryce James, the son of LeBron James, started the first three games of the season for Arizona. Kiyan Anthony, the son of NBA legend Carmelo Anthony, has been a key rotation piece for Syracuse this season. Andrej Stojaković, the son of one of the greatest shooters in NBA history (Peja Stojaković), has played like an All-American this season.

Here are some of the most notable college basketball players playing this season with NBA bloodlines in their family.

Basketball bloodline: Brother of Jeremiah Fears, who plays for the Pelicans

The Fears brothers will have a chance to become the next set of brothers drafted in the first round of the NBA Draft. Jeremiah had a standout one-and-done season at Oklahoma before becoming a lottery pick. Jeremy redshirted during the 2023-24 season after being shot in the leg. Over the last three seasons, Jeremy has emerged as one of the best players in college basketball. He led the nation in assists last season and is on pace to do the same this season.

Basketball bloodline: Son of Peja Stojaković, former NBA All-Star who played for Kings, Pacers, Hornets and Raptors from 1998-2011

Andrej has a completely different skill set than his father, who lit up the NBA in the 2000s as one of the best 3-point shooters in the sport. Andrej is off to an incredible start to the 2026-27 season, highlighted by a 46-point outburst against Duke, in which 12 of his 14 field-goal makes came from inside the arc. Andrej is playing like an All-American this season and is helping Illinois maintain a top-ranked offense without David Mirković in the lineup.

Basketball bloodlines: Son of LeBron James, NBA's all-time leading scorer who currently plays for 76ers, brother of Bronny James, who plays for the Lakers

The son of one of the most famous athletes on the planet began the season as a starter for Arizona while coach Tommy Lloyd was trying to build his rotation in the midst of the RJ Godfrey eligibility dilemma. James does have bragging rights over his older brother and father because he was part of the Wildcats' Final Four roster last season, something no one in his family had done before.

Basketball bloodline: Son of Gilbert Arenas, a three-time NBA All-Star during an NBA career that spanned from 2001-12 with the Warriors, Wizards, Magic and Grizzlies

After playing in 14 games last season, Arenas returned to USC for his sophomore season. It's looking like the right decision. Gilbert's son has developed into one of the best scorers in college basketball, averaging 21.3 points per game. Arenas has also boosted his draft stock tremendously and could be a lottery pick this summer.

Basketball bloodline: Son of Carmelo Anthony, a Syracuse legend who played for Nuggets, Knicks, Thunder, Rockets, Trail Blazers and Lakers from 2003-2022

After appearing in 29 games last season at his father's alma mater, Anthony decided to return to Syracuse for his sophomore season. Anthony is Syracuse's leading scorer (13.5 points per game) despite coming off the bench in all six games this season.

Basketball bloodlines: Son of Carlos Boozer, who played for the Cavaliers, Jazz, Bulls and Lakers from 2002-15; brother of Cameron Boozer, a rookie for the Grizzlies after playing for the Blue Devils last season

With Cameron Boozer declaring for the NBA Draft, this season marked the first time Cayden didn't play on the same team as his brother. Boozer returned to Duke for his sophomore season instead of entering the transfer portal and has started five of his team's first six games this season and is averaging 6.2 points and 4.3 assists.

Basketball bloodline: Son of Scottie Pippen, a Naismith Hall-of-Famer after his 17-season NBA career with the Bulls, Rockets and Trail Blazers

Pippen is at his third school in three seasons after previous stops at Michigan and Cal. In six games at Ohio State, Pippen is averaging 11.5 points, which ranks third on the team. He finished last season as Cal's second-leading scorer before entering the transfer portal.

Basketball bloodlines: Son of Jason Richardson who played for the Warriors, Bobcats, Suns, Magic and 76ers in 14 seasons in NBA; brother of Jase Richardson, who plays for the Magic

Richardson, who was the No. 28-ranked recruit in the 2026 recruiting cycle by 247Sports, has appeared in four games this season for the Crimson Tide. Richardson started the Crimson Tide's season opener against Sam Houston State, where he finished with four points in 15 minutes.

Basketball bloodline: Son of Andre Iguodala, a four-time NBA champion during his career with the 76ers, Nuggets, Warriors and Heat from 2004-23

Iguodala, who was a three-star recruit in the 2025 recruiting cycle by 247Sports, did not appear in a regular season game during his freshman year. However, the son of the former NBA Finals MVP has appeared in four games this season for the Bears.

Basketball bloodline: Son of Trevor Ariza, an 18-year NBA veteran who won an NBA championship with the 2008-09 Lakers

Ariza, who was a four-star recruit in the 2026 recruiting cycle by 247Sports, is currently playing his freshman season at Oregon. Ariza has made four appearances off the bench and is averaging 5.0 points per game.

Basketball bloodline: Brother of DaRon Holmes II, who currently plays for the Nuggets

Holmes, the No. 36 player in the 2026 recruiting cycle by 247Sports, is looking like a key rotational piece for the Wildcats. The brother of the former first-round pick out of Dayton has made six appearances off the bench this season for the No. 8 Wildcats.

Basketball bloodline: Son of Dominique Wilkins, who is in the Naismith Hall of Fame after playing for the Hawks, Clippers, Celtics, Spurs during his long NBA career

The son of one of the greatest dunkers in NBA history made 32 games off the bench for Georgia last season before transferring to play for the Golden Bears. He has started seven games this season for Cal.

Basketball bloodline: Son of Jermaine O'Neal Sr., who played in NBA from 1996-2014 for the Trail Blazers, Pacers and several other teams

The son of the former six-time NBA All-Star is having a breakout season at SMU. After making 34 appearances last season, O'Neal has started all six of SMU's games this season and is averaging 12.3 points per game.

Basketball bloodline: Son of Hakeem Olajuwon, a Naismith Hall-of-Famer after playing for the Rockets and Raptors from 1984-2002

The former four-star recruit has been a key piece for coach Kyle Smith this season. Olajuwon has appeared in six games (four starts) and is averaging 7 points per game. Notably, his younger brother, Malik Olajuwon, committed to and signed with SMU to play next season.

Basketball bloodline: Son of Brandon Bass, who played in the NBA from 2005-17

Bass has made six appearances off the bench thus far during his freshman season at FSU. His best performance came in Florida State's first game, where he dropped 13 points against Florida A&M.

Basketball bloodline: Son of Mo Williams, who played in NBA for 13 seasons, winning an NBA title with the Cavaliers in 2016

Williams is playing his freshman season at the same place where his father is an assistant coach. The former four-star recruit has been a key rotation piece for Mark Pope this season and is averaging 7.2 points off the bench.

Basketball bloodline: Twin brother of Cooper Flagg, who was the No. 1 pick in the NBA Draft after playing for Duke

The twin brother of the No. 1 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft had to wait an extra year to play college basketball. That's because Cooper reclassified to join Duke in time for the 2024-25 season, while his brother played his senior season in high school. After making 32 appearances last season for Maine, mostly off the bench, Ace has started seven games for the Black Bears and is averaging 6.4 points.

Basketball bloodline: Son of Penny Hardaway, a four-time All-Star during his 14-year NBA career

The son of the current Memphis coach has had quite the college journey. He had two separate stints playing for his father at Memphis before transferring to Coastal Carolina this offseason. He has started one game this season at his new school.

Basketball bloodline: Son of Brandon Roy, the Rookie of the Year in 2006-07 while playing for the Trail Blazers before his NBA career ended after a season with the Timberwolves in 2012-13

The son of the former Portland Trail Blazers star is in his second season at Washington. He has appeared in seven total games during his first two seasons at the college level.

Basketball bloodline: Son of Richard Hamilton, who played for the Wizards, Pistons and Bulls from 1999-2013

The son of the former three-time NBA All-Star is in his freshman season at Oakland. He has six appearances off the bench this season.

#2459. NFL Week 12 picks: Our experts face off on Broncos at Steelers, Seahawks at 49ers and more

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Welcome to the most special week in the NFL. We watched the Los Angeles Rams defeat the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night, and now, we have three exciting Thanksgiving matchups to digest this "Turkey Day."

Football fans suffered through many sleepy Chicago Bears vs. Detroit Lions Thanksgiving matchups over the years. Now, this 1 p.m. game on Thursday is expected to be one of the most exciting holiday matchups in recent memory. After that, the Dallas Cowboys will welcome Joe Milton III and the Philadelphia Eagles to AT&T Stadium. Both teams are coming off wins, and the Cowboys need this game if they want to keep pace in the NFC East. At the end of the night, we have a potential AFC Championship preview to watch when the Buffalo Bills host Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. This is just the second game in NFL history to feature two teams coming off at least three straight 17-point victories.

Which teams should you pick in Week 12, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 25 over at DraftKings Sportsbook.

Dajani (Broncos -3.5): Aaron Rodgers lobbed a grenade into the Pittsburgh Steelers facility as he exited it this week. Going on national television and calling your coach a narcoleptic, unhealthy, lazy person who doesn't even know the franchise he works for is insane. So, this is a moment that will ultimately rally the locker room, or cause them to completely fall apart. Pick which side you'd like. The Steelers have also won and covered in six straight home games. This seems like an appropriate time for that streak to end   …  Prediction: Broncos 20, Steelers 13

Dubin (Broncos -3.5): After the disaster that hit the Steelers this week, I just can't see them keeping the game close against the Broncos. No, I don't think they'll get the backup quarterback bounce from Mason Rudolph. I don't trust the Broncos as far as Bo Nix or I can throw them, but given the state the Steelers' locker room has to be in right now, I think you have to roll with Denver to cover this one with relative ease.  … Prediction: Broncos 24, Steelers 10

Dajani (Ravens +7): I have the Houston Texans winning this game, but seven points seems a bit high. C.J. Stroud is playing some great football, but his production has been overshadowed by a defense that has fallen from No. 2 in points allowed per game in 2025, to 17th this year. The Texans are 1-8 against the spread in their last nine home games following an ATS win. I'll take Baltimore to keep it close… Prediction: Texans 24, Ravens 18

Dubin (Ravens +7): The Ravens have now lost six straight, but they've lost the two games in the Jacoby Brissett era by a combined five points despite turning the ball over six times in those contests. If they can just limit the giveaways, I think they might even be able to pull off an upset against a Houston team that hasn't exactly lit the world on fire this year. Either way, I think they can keep it close by throwing on a surprisingly vulnerable Texans pass defense.  … Prediction: Texans 24, Ravens 20

Dajani (49ers -3): Sam Darnold is expected to return this week, and he's accounted for 10 touchdowns compared to nine interceptions in seven starts this season. If you throw out the season opener that Drew Lock finished and won, Darnold is 2-4 as a starter this season.

Believe it or not, San Francisco is 0-9 against the spread in its last nine home divisional games. With the number at a field goal, the 49ers have a good chance to end that streak this week. What they did to the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City last Sunday night was shocking. The 49ers should be headlining everyone's NFL power rankings if they weren't already. Their 0.19 EPA per play is the best mark since the 2018 Chiefs, and they have the best offensive success rate (54.8%) by any team in a season since at least 2000 …  Prediction: 49ers 24, Seahawks 20

Dubin (49ers -3): I reserve the right to flip this prediction to Seattle if Brock Purdy is out with his ankle injury, but if he's in, I just think that this San Francisco offense is a buzzsaw that can't really be stopped — even by the Dark Side defense. Remember, they dropped 32 points on Seattle the last time out. And they've scored 35 or more in each of their three games since returning from the bye. I don't think they can be stopped when everyone is healthy.  … Prediction: 49ers 30, Seahawks 23

Dajani (Raiders +4.5): Maybe part of me is rooting for Fernando Mendoza in his first primetime start? Last week against the Broncos, he threw for 267 yards, three touchdowns and an interception. It was a solid performance, even though the rookie was sacked five times. The Raiders certainly have their weaknesses. They are on pace to become the first team since the 2022 Texans to finish bottom two in both rushing yards per game and opponent rushing yards per game, but this 6-4 Cleveland Browns team hasn't won a game by five-plus points since LAST YEAR. That gives me some optimism Vegas can cover  …  Prediction: Browns 24, Raiders 20

Dubin (Raiders +4.5): I will continue to stand on the idea that this Browns team is not good. Every one of Cleveland's wins has required a game-winning drive in the final minutes of the fourth quarter. The Browns have been out-gained in seven of their 10 games and are somehow 6-4. That is not remotely sustainable. I think the Raiders pull off the upset behind Fernando Mendoza and a returning Brock Bowers. … Prediction: Raiders 21, Browns 17

Dajani (Panthers +3): I'm going to take the points with the Panthers because they are playing on the road. If you were unaware, Carolina is 3-2 away from Charlotte, and has a +8 turnover differential. The Panthers have a -4 turnover differential at home, and allow 37.4 points per game at Bank of America Stadium! For whatever reason, the Panthers are a better team on the road.

It's true that the Tampa Bay Buccaneers throttled the Panthers in Week 7, 43-13, but I think Carolina splits the season series. The Buccaneers are 1-9 against the spread in their last 10 home games, and 0-7 against the spread in their last seven home primetime games. Baker Mayfield is a shocking 1-13 in primetime since 2021, so I'll back Bryce Young …  Prediction: Panthers 28, Buccaneers 27

Dubin (Buccaneers -3): The last time these two teams played, the Bucs racked up 258 rushing yards. The Panthers' run defense then limited the Packers, Broncos and Saints over the next three games, but the Ravens hit them up for 157 yards last week. I don't see much reason to believe that the Bucs will be slowed on the ground, and I don't trust Carolina's offense to score enough to get the Bucs out of their run-heavy orientation.  … Prediction: Buccaneers 20, Panthers 16

Dajani (Bears -1.5): I can't remember being more excited for a Thanksgiving Day game, as the Bears and Lions are two of the best teams in the NFL. What I keep going back to is that the Bears are 6-0 while averaging 33.7 points in games where Caleb Williams starts and finishes. Then, factor in how much improved this Chicago defense looks with the addition of Jeffery Simmons. In Weeks 1-7, they ranked dead last in both yards per play (6.3) and yards per attempt (8.7). Over the last four weeks, the Bears now rank in the top 10 in both categories. Chicago has been swept by Detroit in each of the last two seasons. I think the Bears are done with losing to Dan Campbell …  Prediction: Bears 30, Lions 28

Dubin (Lions +1.5): These are two incredibly evenly-matched teams, but it seems like Detroit has more matchup advantages offensively against Chicago's improved defense than the Bears do against the Lions' own improved unit. With Detroit also getting the benefit of home-field advantage, we're rolling with the Lions to win a close one as a home underdog.  … Prediction: Lions 31, Bears 30

Dajani (Cowboys -8.5): I don't think the Cowboys have exorcised all of their defensive demons just because they blew out the Tennessee Titans, but that win at home was just what this team needed. This is one of those cases where I think the Cowboys just simply out-score their opponent. This is still a rivalry, but the Eagles are 2-8 against the spread this season, which ranks second-worst in the NFL behind the Los Angeles Chargers, and are 0-5 against the spread in their last five divisional matchups. The Cowboys should get this cover in the fourth quarter. They have scored NINETY-ONE (91) points over the past two games! That's the most in a two-game span since 1971…  Prediction: Cowboys 33, Eagles 20

Dubin (Eagles +8.5): I know they just beat the Titans by 21, but I don't like laying this many points with the Cowboys. Their defense is still too suspect and they are still too prone to games where they don't perform up to expectations for me to be comfortable with an 8.5-point spread. So even while I think they'll dent the scoreboard at home on Thanksgiving afternoon, I can't bring myself to predict that this will be a blowout. … Prediction: Cowboys 30, Eagles 24

Dajani (Chiefs +3): The craziest part about this rivalry is that the Bills have won the last five regular-season meetings, while the Chiefs have won the last four playoff meetings! You should also know that the weather is supposed to be terrible on Thursday night, so this could come down to which team runs the ball better. James Cook has recorded nine straight games with 75 rushing yards and a touchdown. He and Josh Allen are the second duo to ever account for double-digit rushing touchdowns each through the first 10 games of a season. Meanwhile, on the other side, Emmett Johnson has rushed for 206 yards with 108 receiving yards and three touchdowns over the last two games in place of the injured Kenneth Walker III. I almost think a three-point spread in this matchup is pretty high. That's going to lead me to take the points even though Bills over Chiefs has been an auto-bet in the regular season recently… Prediction: Chiefs 17, Bills 16

Dubin (Bills -3): I have basically the exact same analysis of this game as Dajani but come down on the opposite side of the bet because of the Bills' regular-season history against the Chiefs and the relative strength of their run game. I trust Josh Allen and James Cook to run the ball more than I do Emmett Johnson, even with how good Johnson has been over the last two weeks. Could Patrick Mahomes make this prediction look silly? Of course. But I think that'll prove more difficult in Thursday night's expected weather. … Prediction: Bills 21, Chiefs 17

#2457. Te voorzichtig of een gevolg van het WK-format? Nederland-Japan 2:2

von Next Generation am 19.06.2026 in den Kategorien National Teams,Uncategorized mit 1 Kommentar

De twee favorieten van de groep stonden tegenover elkaar. “Dat regelen we wel in de andere wedstrijden” had zomaar het motto van beide ploegen kunnen zijn.

Nederland speelde tegen Japan in balbezit vanuit een duidelijke 1-4-3-3-basisformatie, met zeer lage backs, duidelijke spelers die voor de breedte zorgden, een echte spits (Malen) en twee nummers tien (Rijnders en Gravenberch).

Japan verdedigde vanuit een 1-5-4-1-middenblok, stuurde het spel naar buiten en zette alleen bij Nederlandse doeltrappen hoger druk. Om vanuit het middenblok over te schakelen naar een actiever, meer sturend middenblok met druk op de flank, schoof Maeda aan de linkerkant (op papier de linker tien in het 1-5-4-1) door naar de eerste pressinglijn en zette hij samen met wingback Nakamura druk op Dumfries. Daardoor werd De Jong vaak als vrije nummer zes losjes afgeschermd door de Japanse dubbele zes en de zeer terugverdedigende spits Ueda. Japan zette zijn pressing alleen heel situationeel in, goed afgestemd tussen de voorste en middelste lijn, wanneer een breedtepass gevolgd werd door een korte terugpass. Daardoor waren zowel de actie als de vervolgactie goed te voorspellen en waren de passlijnen kort en makkelijk te belopen.

Nederlandse controlfreaks met één uitzondering

Voor Nederland lag in balbezit, binnen het zeer positievaste en vooral statische 1-4-3-3, een sterke focus op controle in de wedstrijd. Daarbij werden ook de technisch sterke centrale verdedigers met korte passafstanden nadrukkelijk betrokken als opbouwers. In veel oefenwedstrijden en Nations League-duels vormde Van de Ven als linksback vaak een soort driemansopbouw doordat hij laag bleef, terwijl Dumfries hoger doorschoof. Tegen diepere of passievere blokken ontstond zo vaak een soort 1-3-2-4-1. In deze wedstrijd bleef echter ook Dumfries in het begin vrijwel uitsluitend onderdeel van de opbouwlijn. Naarmate de wedstrijd vorderde werd Dumfries, in tegenstelling tot Nederland als geheel, wel moediger en schoof hij af en toe door naar de halfspace of zelfs zonder bal mee de zestien in.

Voor De Jong, die zoals altijd heel dicht bij de opbouwlijn zijn positie koos, maakten beide achten die tussen de Japanse linies speelden zoveel mogelijk ruimte vrij. De Nederlandse opbouwlijn probeerde de afstand voor de Japanse voorste lijn te vergroten door met een vlakke viermansopbouw te spelen. Daarbij lieten ze af en toe zien welke kwaliteit er door het centrum mogelijk is, vooral via Van Dijk en De Jong (soms samen met een tijdelijk terugzakkende Rijnders), wanneer ze druk kunnen uitlokken door de grote afstanden van de backs en vervolgens centraal door kunnen spelen.

Japan was zich daar echter van bewust en liet zich maar zelden verleiden. Daardoor speelde Nederland steeds opnieuw in een grote “U” rond het Japanse blok. Nederland nam geen risicovolle beslissingen en gebruikte balbezit vooral als verdedigend middel om geen fouten te maken of Japanse counters weg te geven. Een veelgebruikte toernooitactiek voor technisch en individueel sterkere teams.

Door het overtal in de opbouw en de focus op simpele passes werden gevaarlijke balverliezen in het centrum vermeden, ondersteund door een degelijke restverdediging. Maar zo extreem als hier — met een vlakke viermansopbouw, extreem positievaste tienen (geen overbelasting, niet actief om de bal vragen) en vrijwel geen dribbels behalve van de brede buitenspelers in hogere posities — bleef vooral de vraag hoe Nederland zelf kansen wilde creëren.

Een terugkerend, bijna consequent patroon in de Nederlandse opbouw was het bewust opschuiven via de linkerkant. Vooral Gakpo werd vaak in één-tegen-één-situaties gebracht dankzij goede bindende loopacties van Rijnders. Gakpo koos echter niet voor een directe actie tegen zijn tegenstander, maar juist voor een licht vertragende dribbel met als doel een vrije passhoek naar binnen te creëren. Dat had ook een nadeel: extra Japanse spelers konden achter de bal komen en ruimtes afsluiten in zijn één-tegen-één.

De reden daarvoor lag in het Nederlandse idee om Donyell Malen, die zich tijdens de opbouw nauwelijks met het spel bemoeide, in de voeten aan te spelen. Daar kon hij met zijn wendbaarheid goed standhouden en was hij vervelend om te verdedigen.

Aan de andere kant werd er via de rechterkant langzaam opgebouwd. Dat gebeurde door een klassieke positiewisseling tussen Summerville en Dumfries of via lange diagonale verplaatsingen van Van Dijk naar Summerville, steeds met oog voor een goede verdedigende positie.

Malen had ook vaker al eerder tijdens de opbouw gezocht of aangespeeld kunnen worden. Maar of hij die momenten zelf niet herkende, of dat de Nederlandse aanpak van defensief balbezit dit simpelweg niet toeliet, blijft de vraag.

Daarom begon Gravenberch al vrij vroeg als balverre nummer tien de centrale ruimtes achter de Japanse dubbele zes te bezetten. Zijn ploeggenoten deden echter weinig met die bewegingen — bijvoorbeeld door kort naar binnen te dribbelen of doordat Rijnders uitweek — waardoor Gravenberch daar uiteindelijk weer mee stopte.

Eenvoud als middel om fouten te vermijden had zomaar het oranje motto van deze wedstrijd kunnen zijn.

Toch ontstond de beste Nederlandse aanval juist door meer risico te nemen. Een pass tussen de linies naar Gravenberch, een dribbel in een 1-tegen-2, een overlap van Dumfries waardoor de 1-tegen-1 van Summerville veranderde in een 2-tegen-1 en uiteindelijk een vrije schietkans ontstond. Allemaal elementen die veel te weinig terugkwamen in deze wedstrijd.

Wanneer Japan nog verder terugzakte in een extreem compact 5-4-1-blok rond het eigen strafschopgebied, positioneerden de Nederlandse backs zich iets meer diagonaal tussen centrale verdediger en buitenspeler en kwamen ze dus iets meer naar binnen.

Verdedigend koos Nederland bij Japanse doeltrappen voor een zeer mangeoriënteerde aanpak. Ze stuurden de Japanse opbouw naar de zwakkere voet van de speler aan de bal om zo een zo onnauwkeurig mogelijke lange bal en een luchtduel uit te lokken. In de lucht hadden de Nederlanders immers een duidelijk voordeel.

Voor de rest liet Nederland zich meestal terugzakken in een vrij passieve 1-5-4-1, waarbij De Jong vaak de laatste lijn aanvulde om Doan, Kubo of de rechter tien van Japan te volgen.

Nederland was heel duidelijk gefocust op het afdekken van de diepte en wilde absoluut geen ruimte achter of voor de verdediging weggeven. Daardoor kwam de Nederlandse dubbele zes in een lastig dilemma terecht tussen hun mandekking en de verticale compactheid ten opzichte van de laatste lijn van Oranje, die in twijfelgevallen eerder achteruit dan vooruit verdedigde.

Een enkele spits in een 1-5-4-1 heeft het meestal moeilijk, maar Malen probeerde ook niet echt functies op zich te nemen die zijn ploeg konden helpen. Tegelijk waren de buitenste spelers van het blok vooral bezig met hun verticale mandekking op de Japanse driemansopbouw. Daardoor zette Nederland vrijwel geen druk op de Japanse opbouw, die zich vrij kon ontwikkelen.

Het zeer beweeglijke en rotatierijke aanvalsspel van Japan tegenover de fysieke, grote Nederlandse spelers liet vooral potentieel zien wanneer Japan vroeg naar de flank speelde en vervolgens naar binnen combineerde.

Door het gebrek aan druk van Nederland kon Japan vanuit de opbouwlijn schone en snelle passcombinaties uitvoeren naar een hoog gepositioneerde wingback. Vanaf daar kon die relatief eenvoudig naar binnen spelen, omdat de pressingafstanden van de Nederlandse backs te groot waren om al bij de eerste aanname druk te zetten.

Kort gezegd kon Japan, door de — in deze context — veel te late druk van Nederland, sneller en zuiverder naar de flank spelen dan Nederland in staat was om daar druk op te krijgen. Want als de Nederlandse backs eerder zouden uitstappen, zouden ze veel verder naar buiten worden getrokken, wat weer haaks stond op het Nederlandse idee om het centrum en de diepte gesloten te houden.

Vanaf de flank kon Japan vervolgens profiteren van het eerder beschreven dilemma van de Nederlandse dubbele zes. Die moest nu kiezen tussen het blijven volgen van hun directe tegenstander (zoals Rijnders vaak deed), waardoor ruimte vóór de verdediging ontstond, of terugzakken richting de laatste lijn, waardoor er voor hen geen druk meer op de bal was.

Door verloren één-tegen-één-duels in het centrum, problemen in het volgen van tegenstanders en de algemene passiviteit van het blok kwam Japan uiteindelijk ook op gelijke hoogte. Na een gebrek aan duidelijke afspraken bij het winnen van terrein konden de Japanners het strafschopgebied binnendringen en werden ze tot aan het schot eigenlijk alleen maar begeleid.

Ironisch genoeg werd juist Dumfries’ actieve manier van verdedigen hem fataal, omdat hij zijn benen opende en daarmee de korte hoek vrijgaf voor Nakamura.

Daar kwam nog bij dat naast De Jong ook Van Hecke en vooral Van Dijk moeite hadden met korte, diepe loopacties. Mede door het gebrek aan afdekking hadden ze problemen om die goed te volgen.

Door gebrekkige timing en onvoldoende precisie wist Japan daar uiteindelijk niet optimaal van te profiteren. Omdat De Jong geen natuurlijke centrale verdediger is, werd de diepte soms niet goed bewaakt door de laatste lijn. Daarnaast kozen Van Dijk en Van Hecke geregeld een andere hoogte dan De Jong, iets wat Japan eigenlijk te weinig uitbuitte.

Een kleine aanpassing die weinig opleverde

In de loop van de wedstrijd paste Nederland de aanloophoeken aan. Daardoor veranderde automatisch ook de positie van de buitenste spelers van de middenlinie. Zij konden nu iets losser uit de lijn stappen richting de hoog opgeschoven Japanse wingbacks en druk zetten op indribbelende of terugzakkende Japanse opbouwers. Zo kon Japan minder makkelijk direct naar de flank spelen zoals eerder beschreven.

Toch klopten zowel het moment als de richting van die acties niet. Daardoor stonden spelers als Gakpo en Koopmeiners hoger op het veld, maar konden ze na een succesvolle Japanse pass niet meer meeverdedigen in dezelfde actie.

In plaats daarvan hingen ze vaak een beetje tussen wal en schip. Opmerkelijk genoeg sloten ze niet de terugpass af — wat de één-tegen-één-verdediging op de flank juist geholpen zou hebben — maar probeerden ze alsnog aansluiting te houden bij de actie. Daardoor kregen de Japanse wingbacks juist meer ruimte aan de zijkant en werd ook het verleggen van het spel makkelijker.

Grotere defensieve problemen ontstonden ook wanneer de Nederlandse flankduo’s rotaties moesten verdedigen, vooral aan de kant van Gakpo. Waar Koopmeiners kwaliteiten heeft in het volgen van zijn directe tegenstander, verloor Gakpo af en toe zijn man uit het oog.

Opvallend kwetsbaar was Nederland bovendien in de organisatie van de verdediging bij corners en ingooien.

Bij de weinige balveroveringen waren zowel de besluitvorming als de omschakelkracht van Nederland te zwak om echt gevaarlijk te worden.

Daarnaast werd de horizontale compactheid in de slotfase steeds slechter, waardoor Japan steeds vaker vrije spelers tussen de linies vond. De vraag is of dat vooral een fysiek probleem was of eerder een cognitief en organisatorisch probleem

De verdedigende strategie versterkte en veroorzaakte individuele probleme

Ook De Jongs manier van dekken past niet echt bij de zeer directe en doorjagende stijl van Van Dijk en Van Hecke. Waar die twee hun tegenstander vanuit de laatste lijn vaak strak blijven volgen, houdt De Jong zich als balverre speler vaker bezig met het (her)organiseren van de verdediging. Daardoor ontstaan er vrije spelers tussen de linies, zeker omdat de Nederlandse dubbele zes ook nog eens mangeoriënteerd verdedigt.

Wanneer De Jong wél uitstapt uit de laatste lijn, laat hij soms problemen zien in het daadwerkelijk druk zetten, vooral qua dynamiek nadat hij de eerste aanname van zijn tegenstander heeft verdedigd. Japan maakte daar richting het einde van de wedstrijd meerdere keren gebruik van om de balcirculatie in hogere zones netjes voort te zetten en het spel te verleggen.

Later in de wedstrijd werd De Jong vervangen door Aké.

Ook aan de andere kant viel op dat vooral Van Dijk moeite had met het oppakken en volgen van de snelle wisselbewegingen van de Japanners, met name bij korte bewegingen in de diepte (zie afbeelding). Door zijn directe, mangeoriënteerde manier van verdedigen kwam hij daarbij af en toe in de problemen. Japan wist daar echter niet van te profiteren door een gebrek aan timing en precisie. Over het geheel genomen waren er dus meerdere individual-tactische tekortkomingen zichtbaar die niet goed aansloten bij de gekozen passieve verdedigende strategie.

In balbezit beschikt Nederland over veel individuele kwaliteit. Als een tegenstander in de val loopt, kan Nederland via alle spelers in het centrum dynamiek creëren. De aanpak van defensief balbezit was echter behoorlijk extreem en zorgde voor weinig doelkansen, maar wel voor veel controle over de wedstrijd.

Waarschijnlijk was het plan om Malen vaker vrij te spelen vanaf de flank en hem zo beter in het spel te betrekken. Desondanks heeft Nederland, zelfs met kleine aanpassingen waarbij iets meer risico wordt genomen, enorm veel potentie om gevaarlijk aanvallend voetbal te spelen en tegen iedere tegenstander tot kansen en doelpunten te komen.

Wat vanuit Nederlands perspectief eerder zorgen zou moeten baren, is de defensieve organisatie. De balans tussen druk zetten en het afsluiten van het centrum en de tussenruimtes klopt niet. De druk ligt op zo’n laag prioriteitsniveau dat voor iedere degelijke ploeg op dit toernooi het vinden van de juiste veldbezetting en het opschuiven geen echte uitdaging vormt. De sluitende bewegingen van de Nederlandse spelers zorgen daardoor eerder voor schadebeperking dan voor het daadwerkelijk voorkomen van gevaar. Hun bewegingen worden als het ware zonder enige vorm van druk volledig geneutraliseerd.

Ook de laatste lijn en de verdediging van het eigen strafschopgebied ogen niet extreem goed op elkaar afgestemd. Problemen in de mandekkingen op de flank, vrijwel geen mogelijkheden om te counteren vanwege de lage en op mandekking gebaseerde posities, en een algemene slaperigheid bij standaardsituaties kunnen Nederland al in de groepsfase flink parten spelen.

In Nederland zorgde de invalbeurt van Depay bij een stand van 2-1 voor veel verbazing onder de toeschouwers. In werkelijkheid wist hij niet echt acties toe te voegen die Oranje verder hielpen.

Wel moet worden gezegd dat de positie van enige spits voor een diep, naar achteren gericht en passief 1-5-4-1-blok tegen een tegenstander die opbouwt in een 3-2-structuur weinig invloedrijke mogelijkheden biedt.

Toch zou een dynamischere spits, die meer loopt en diepgang brengt, Nederland vooral bij balveroveringen en omschakelmomenten waarschijnlijk meer hebben geholpen dan Depay in deze wedstrijd deed

HH groeide op aan de Nederlands-Duitse grens, maar keek op tactisch vlak liever richting Zuid-Europa. Naast zijn werkzaamheden als freelancer voor Duitse profclubs is hij sinds twee jaar ook actief als jeugdtrainer bij de O17 van N.E.C. Nijmegen.

LL ontdekte zijn fascinatie voor voetbalinhoud en tactiek dankzij de vernieuwende ideeën van Tuchel bij Mainz. In de regio rond de Narrenstadt is hij al actief geweest binnen zowel het amateurvoetbal als de jeugdopleidingen van profclubs (NLZ).

#2456. La Scaloneta, a rejuvenated Argentina, are on course for 2022 World Cup glory

Whilst European champions Italy and Cristiano Ronaldo’s Portugal must sweat it out in next March’s World Cup playoffs, Lionel Scaloni’s Argentina side have serenely booked their tickets to Qatar for the tournament after a 0–0 draw with Brazil in San Juan.

By clinching their place in the World Cup with five qualifiers still to play, the team dubbed “La Scaloneta” in the Argentine press have not only avoided the tortuous qualifying campaigns of the last two World Cups, but also completed a dream year. They ended 2021 on a 27-game unbeaten run and ended a 28-year-long racha (losing streak) without a major trophy by winning the Copa América in July.

Having lost six tournament finals during this luckless run dating back to 1993, Lionel Scaloni’s men finally managed to scratch the itch afflicting Argentine football fans for almost three decades when they beat arch-rivals Brazil in their own backyard of the Maracanã in Rio in the final.

Whilst most of the attention inevitably fell on Lionel Messi’s first senior trophy victory in the Albiceleste jersey of his country after the heartbreak of losing in four tournament finals, Argentina’s unsung hero win was coach Scaloni, who modestly said in the post-match press conference that anyone else in his position would have achieved the same result, hailing instead his ’28 warriors’.

Scaloni’s transition from relative unknown to national hero is the stuff of fairy stories. His playing career began at Newell’s Old Boys in Scaloni’s home city of Rosario, and he was a member of the Argentine team that won the 1997 Under-20 World Cup in Malaysia alongside the likes of Pablo Aimar and Walter Samuel, who also form part of Scaloni’s coaching team.

Scaloni later moved to Deportivo in Spain, where he spent the majority of his career, playing 200 games for the Galicians. The right-back found prominence in England during a six-month loan spell with West Ham in 2006 when his consistent performances helped the Hammers reach the FA Cup final against Liverpool, as well as a surprise call-up to the Argentine squad for the World Cup in Germany that year ahead of Javier Zanetti.

After retiring as a player in 2015, Scaloni began his coaching career a year later as assistant to compatriot, Jorge Sampaoli at Sevilla, following the latter in the same role when he took charge of the national team in 2017.

After Argentina’s chaotic and disastrous 2018 World Cup campaign ended with the departure of the hapless Sampaoli, the AFA turned to Scaloni, a relative coaching rookie to stabilise the country’s international football reputation whilst they found a permanent replacement.

Whilst there was a wealth of Argentine coaching talent available in the shape of Diego Simeone, Mauricio Pochettino and Marcelo Gallardo, the AFA were in no position financially to tempt any of them from existing positions at Atlético, Tottenham and River Plate whilst paying severance to Sampaoli who had signed a lucrative, long-term contract just a year before.

Charged with rejuvenating an aging squad, Scaloni made positive early progress in terms introducing an organised style of play, something that was completely lacking in Russia where the players are rumoured to have picked the team. As veterans such as Javier Mascherano and Gonzalo Higuaín retired from international football, others like Marcos Rojo, Gabriel Mercado and Éver Banega were jettisoned by Scaloni, who created a new team based on midfielders Giovanni Lo Celso, Leandro Paredes and Rodrigo De Paul, and Inter striker Lautaro Martínez.

In terms of style, Scaloni made clear that tactically he was his own man. He outlined a preference for a more direct style of play, with a quick transition from defence to attack that had proved successful for France and Croatia at the 2018 World Cup, saying “it’s the style I like and it’s the moment to implant it in Argentina”, a contrast to the long-favoured preference in the country for a short-passing game built up from the midfield.

Scaloni’s first competitive challenge as caretaker came with the 2019 Copa América in Brazil. Whilst Argentina lost their opening game against Colombia in which they employed two wingers, Scaloni showed his tactical pragmatism – a feature of his time in charge of La Albiceleste – to correct his mistakes and restore the team to winning ways. Argentina qualified from their group, beat Venezuela 2–0 in the quarter-final and were unlucky to bow out to hosts Brazil in the semi following some dubious refereeing decisions.

On the strength of the progress made in Brazil, Scaloni’s reward was to have his position made permanent ahead of the 2022 World Cup qualifiers and the 2020 Copa América in which Argentina were slated to be co-hosts with Colombia. The COVID-19 pandemic saw the latter competition postponed to 2021 but, after co-hosts Colombia succumbed to social unrest and with COVID-19 levels at chronic levels in Argentina, CONMEBOL made a last-minute decision to move the Copa América to Brazil – which was hardly in a more suitable position to host the competition – arguably taking some of the pressure off Scaloni.

With just two World Cup qualifiers to fine-tune his team ahead of the tournament in which the team flew in and out of Brazil immediately before and after matches, whilst staying at their Ezeiza training complex near the airport, where the squad bonded over barbecues and reggaeton music, with popular winger Papu Gómez acting as head of entertainment.

Indeed, those two qualifiers helped Scaloni identify the missing pieces of his defensive jigsaw that helped Argentina concede just three goals on their way to Copa glory. In goal, Emiliano Martínez, who had enjoyed a stellar rise over the previous year from journeyman to FA Cup-winner and one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League, became the reliable keeper that Argentina had been seeking more years.

The Villa man’s confidence was highlighted by his heroics and sledging of opposition players during the decisive semi-final shootout against Colombia in the semi-final as he brought to mind Sergio Goycochea’s similar role in Argentina’s 1991 and 1993 triumphs.

Meanwhile, in Atalanta centre-half Cristian Romero, Scaloni has found a strong, pacy defender to act as the rock of the defence, despite injury hindering his participation in the competition.

If one thing has stood out about Scaloni’s Argentina, it has been the togetherness and absence of egos – not a familiar trait in Argentine teams of the recent past. Each player had a clear sense of both individual and collective responsibility, not least in the Copa final against Brazil in which Scaloni’s game plan was executed perfectly as players like Emi Martínez, Romero and, most notably, Rodrigo De Paul showed themselves to be leaders on the pitch.

It has also been an atmosphere in which Messi has flourished. Previously criticised when playing for the national team for a perceived lack of patriotism, and for playing as though he had the weight of the world was on his shoulders, Messi has been a man reborn. He now sings the national anthem lustily and plays with a previously unseen freedom and sense of enjoyment that saw him finish as Copa Player of the Tournament.

Speaking of his captain who gave gave everything despite playing with a hamstring injury in the semi and final, Scaloni said, “I believe that he identified with this team, that he could win or lose without lowering his shoulders.”

Scaloni’s achievements have set the tone for Argentina being serious contenders to win the World Cup in Qatar in what could be Messi’s last hurrah in an Argentine shirt. It is something the coach is already planning for, claiming that it is important that he is transparent in affirming that nobody has their place assured as looks ahead to the reality of a post-Messi future.

As such, Scaloni has left the door open to youngsters from the Olympic team like Alexis McAllister, Julián Álvarez and Pedro de la Vega to force their way into his plans, whilst established stars such as Paulo Dybala and Mauro Icardi, who have never fully delivered at international level, will similarly be given the opportunity to make their case. One thing is for sure, Scaloni now deserves to receive the plaudits for what he has achieved for Argentine football.

#2455. Prisco's Week 12 NFL picks: Browns over Raiders, Steelers overcome issues to upset Broncos

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

That's three consecutive winning weeks for me, which is a big positive. I was 7-6 against the spread last week and 9-4 straight up. My straight-up record is now 104-58-1, while my ATS record is 75-85-3.

I can see .500 now after being buried under it at the start of the season.

This is Thanksgiving Week, which is usually a good week for me. And I feel good about the picks.

It starts Wednesday night with a good one between the Packers and Rams, and it ends Monday night with the Bucs against the Panthers. I really like the teams in both of those games.

We have NFL games Wednesday, Thursday (Thanksgiving), Friday, Sunday and Monday. What a feast.

I know I will as the climb to .500 ATS continues.

This Friday game pits two teams who would be in the playoffs right now. But the Steelers have lost two straight and haven't looked good. Denver has won six in a row. But I think the Steelers will find a way to show up and win this one behind their running game. It won't be pretty, but the Steelers will find a way.

The Bengals are coming off a tough road loss at Washington, while the Saints are playing consecutive road games. The Bengals offense didn't score as it had in Monday's game, but that will change here. Joe Burrow gets back on track. Bengals big.

The Giants are coming off an impressive victory over the Jaguars, while the Colts are coming off a bye. They released quarterback Daniel Jones, which means Anthony Richardson will be starting. The Giants' defense should dominate in this one. The Colts have packed it in, so the Giants take it.

The Jets are playing consecutive road games, while the Dolphins are home for the first time in three weeks. The Jets played well in beating the Chargers last week, while Miami lost to the Bills. The Dolphins are limited on offense, but the Jets' defense has struggled. Look for Miami to hang around.

The Vikings are home after getting blown out by the 49ers in Mexico. The Falcons are off a bye. The Minnesota offense struggled against the 49ers, but the Falcons have had defensive problems lately. Look for the Minnesota defense to get back on track as well. Vikings take it.

The Jaguars are coming off a bad showing in the loss to the Giants, while Tennessee gave up 51 to the Cowboys last week. Ouch. The Jaguars scored 40 against them two weeks ago. They won't get that many here, but it will still be ugly as Trevor Lawrence and the passing game get back on track.

This is essentially a playoff game of sorts for these two. The loser is pretty much done. The Texans are home off a Thursday game, while the Ravens are playing consecutive road games. Edge Houston. The Texans have played well on offense, and the Ravens' defense is a mess. Look for a big day for C.J. Stroud.

This was once scheduled for prime time, but it was moved because both teams have flopped this year. The Patriots will start Tommy DeVito for the injured Drake Maye. That's a problem. The Chargers might not have Justin Herbert (concussion) either, which would put D.J. Uiagalelei in as the starter. He's thrown seven passes in his career. Even so, give me the home team here.

The Commanders are coming off an impressive home victory Monday night over the Bengals, while the Cardinals got rocked by the Chiefs last week. Arizona has big-time issues and fired the defensive coordinator this week. That defense will struggle to stop Jayden Daniels. The Commanders stay hot.

The 49ers have the best record in the NFC and seem to be cruising to the division title. But Seattle can slow that talk down here with a victory. That will be tough to do on the road. Look for a lower-scoring game in the second division game between the two — the 49ers won the first — and San Francisco will win it late.

This has been flexed to prime time because the Browns would be a playoff team right now. Plus, the Raiders have rookie Fernando Mendoza making his third start. The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, and Cleveland is off a bye. Big edge to the Browns as they win it behind their defense.

The Panthers can take a stronghold on the division with a victory here.  They come in with defensive issues, but the Bucs have problems in the passing game. So what gives? I think the Tampa Bay defense will play well here and the Bucs will run it right at Carolina to win it like they did in the first meeting.

Dak Prescott has thrown nine touchdown passes and no picks in the past two weeks. The Dallas offense is rolling. The Eagles defense will be a challenge. Joe Milton, who was on the Cowboys' practice squad, will start at quarterback for the Eagles. Dallas will play better defense against him this week. Cowboys big.

This is the game of the week. Patrick Mahomes vs. Josh Allen. What's not to like as two of the best in the league go at it? The Bills have played much better defense lately, but they've faced a bunch of backup quarterbacks. Not here. So look for both passers to have good days. In the end, Allen will make the big play late to win it.

This should be an offensive show. Both teams can score, even if Chicago hasn't been great on offense the past two games. On this fast track, look out. The Bears defense has played well since getting Jeffrey Simmons in a trade, but they won't stop the Lions here. Look for a lot of points with the home team getting the victory on Thanksgiving.

The Packers get Micah Parsons back, while the Rams will be without Puka Nacua for the rest of the season. Their offense is limited without him. But this game will be decided by how well the Packers' line can block Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett. They've been bad, but I think they will be better here. The defense will keep this close, and Jordan Love will win it late.

#2454. NBA Power Rankings: Knicks making their move as Karl-Anthony Towns has taken center stage

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The New York Knicks may have cut off contract extension talks with Karl-Anthony Towns before the season, but Towns is doing plenty of negotiating on his own behalf with his play. Towns has been extraordinary for a Knicks team that still hasn't found its top form after winning the title, but is trending that way with five straight wins to get to 11-6.

Towns leads the league with 13.9 rebounds per game. It's not just his size; he is a technician on the glass with the way he gets into the body of his man to stop his forward momentum and then almost springs himself back toward the ball for a two-birds-with-one-stone maneuver.

Meanwhile, Towns is averaging 21.8 of just about the most efficient points possible for a shooting big man at 54% overall and 41.5% on five 3s a game. His 15 straight double-doubles to start the season are a Knicks record. It's unlikely that he'll reach Bill Walton's all-time mark of 34 straight double-doubles to start the 1976-77 season, but with the way he's playing, you can't rule anything out.

Towns now has 20 straight regular-season doubles dating back to last year, four times more than the next highest active streak (Victor Wembanyama currently has five straight). Towns gets to his 3s in every way. He pops. Stretches. His step-back is about the only thing not going for him at present, but it's a nasty weapon with how dangerous he is as a driver.

It's tempting to think Towns should be firing off even more 3s, but he is so dialed in on his attack times and zones that it's best to just let him continue playing on balance. When Jalen Brunson is in, he steps back. When Brunson is out, he ramps up the scoring. He's become the best high-hub passer this side of Nikola Jokić; no dime is too ambitious for him, as he is into full anticipatory quarterbacking rather than waiting for things to show open, which marks the highest level of facilitation.

Get it to Towns at the top and cut, and you've got a good chance for a bucket:

KAT continues to hoop, good cut from Landry pic.twitter.com/5FG2CAKkGg

KAT with the beautiful assist to Josh Hart for an easy 2.Can you imagine how fun playing basketball with KAT must be? pic.twitter.com/5L9QwYR2N8

Watch here as the Knicks flank Towns with a pair of two-man screening actions on each side. The first one, on his right, doesn't yield anything. But like a quarterback, he keeps going through his progressions until a second source produces fruit.

On a retrouvé le dilemme mortelle des Playoffs 2026 sur les actions autour de KAT le playmaker :Balle plein centre et deux jeux à deux de chaque côté.Ne switchez pas, et c'est un cut ouvert pour OG pic.twitter.com/TmIIB0yNfk

These cuts are open for the Knicks because Towns, first, has pulled the big man away from the basket, and even more when Brunson is on the court and the defense has to be so concerned with the two-man handoffs that the lid is completely lifted.

From there, Towns is a triple threat, weaponized as both a passer (four assists a game and almost six more potential assists), screener (55 screen assists), and of course as a driver when he sees the open lane.

BIG KAT IS SO BACKOn lui donne le ballon dans l'elbow 👉Rip screen de Brunson pour Bridges qui ne donne rien 👉Fake DHO de KAT ce qui surprend Gobert et donc peut aller jusqu'au panier et finir ! Et comme Rudy était placé sur KAT = aucune protection de cercle derrière. pic.twitter.com/zFb4YHSaWO

Notice how Towns doesn't just put the ball on the floor right away. He is so tuned into the off-ball movement. I know I keep using the quarterback analogy, but it's really what it is. He has the mobility to tuck the ball and run himself, but his first priority is more often to wait for his receivers to open up. His feel for when, where and how to attack has become surgical.

The Knicks don't want to cross the second apron. Nobody does. They have to pay or lose Towns, Josh Hart, Miles McBride and Tyler Kolek. Maybe they all accept a little haircut to keep the band together. But if it comes down to it, Towns has proven himself to be completely irreplaceable. There is no other center who can provide what he does, particularly in the context of his team. Towns has mastered the star/sidekick toggle alongside Brunson.

The Knicks might have shut off negotiations, but Towns effectively stayed at the table. Now it's his game doing all the talking. And it's saying only one thing.

PAY THAT MAN HIS MONEY!!!! pic.twitter.com/QN0AIv9TsX

#2453. Jerry Jones refutes Aaron Rodgers' accusations, calls Mike McCarthy 'outstanding'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

ARLINGTON, Texas -- Aaron Rodgers nuked Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy's reputation after the Steelers benched him late Tuesday night.

In a scathing appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" on ESPN on Wednesday, the four-time NFL MVP and Super Bowl XLV MVP ripped McCarthy, saying Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth told him of Pittsburgh's decision to make him inactive for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos, and he accused McCarthy of sleeping and being late to team meetings throughout the season. Rodgers raised numerous other accusations against McCarthy, including that he arrived late this week and slept during offensive meetings.

Rodgers said that the behavior McCarthy exhibited this season in Pittsburgh was present during their shared tenure with the Green Bay Packers, as well as during McCarthy's run as head coach of the Dallas Cowboys. The Cowboys employed McCarthy as their head coach for five seasons from 2020 to 2024, and they went 49-35 in that span, tied for the eighth-best record in the league with the Minnesota Vikings. Dallas won 12 games in the regular season for three consecutive years from 2021 to 2023, the first time the franchise accomplished that feat since their 1990s Super Bowl dynasty teams. The Cowboys went 1-3 in the postseason under McCarthy, advancing no further than the NFC divisional round.

"They know what's going on. Like I said, they all know. Everybody knows," Rodgers said on Wednesday. "Just like the guys in Green Bay knew. It's like the people in Dallas knew. Like they know what the deal is."

One of the people in Dallas who claimed not to know what Rodgers was talking about is Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones. Jones unequivocally refuted Rodgers' claims and said he tried to extend McCarthy when his original five-year contract expired at the end of the 2024 season. The two sides couldn't come to an agreement on a new deal, so McCarthy took a year off in 2025 before being hired by the Steelers this year.

"I never saw anything that would not ... I offered him to stay at least another year when he left. I thought he was outstanding as the head coach, and [he] had a great command of quarterback, offense. Can't say enough good things about him. He's frankly one of the finest people around football that I have been around. I can't say enough about him. I never had the type of thing that's being said about him, I've never had that in consideration at any of my time with him. [Whether it was] extending his contract or any of that. That [alleged behavior] was never on the table."

While Rodgers painted a picture of extremely erratic and irresponsible behavior by his longtime head coach, Jones claims none of that happened in Dallas.

#2451. NFL Thanksgiving overreactions: Bears a shoo-in for NFC North title? Should Joe Milton be a full-time QB1?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

You're probably on your second or third nap by now, right? No, we're not saying you're Mike McCarthy, nor are we saying you could coach the Pittsburgh Steelers (or Green Bay Packers, for that matter). We're merely pointing out that you've consumed enough tryptophan from the Thanksgiving turkey that you're probably a little lethargic. And if that means you dozed off during some of the NFL's Thanksgiving triple-header, that's alright. We're here to help you sift through what went down over the holiday slate and make you sound smart.

Given that all three games were in individual windows and the entire nation was huddled around the table to watch them, there will be a lot of opinions that spew out of them. Some will be justified, while others you'll rightfully tilt your head, squint your eyebrows, and judge silently. We'll make you the former.

Below, we'll go through some of the top storylines from each Thanksgiving game and determine if they're something to take seriously or if they're merely overreactions.

When it comes to statement wins, you won't find many bigger than the Bears rolling into Ford Field and pulling off the 39-35 win over the Lions. Chicago scored the game-winning touchdown with just three seconds left in regulation and erased an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit. That victory puts the Bears at 9-2 on the season, and that has them atop the NFC North.

THAT'S A TOUCHDOWN!!!!!!📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/IOUvYvWOHa

Naturally, confidence is sky-high that Chicago will eventually secure the division title for the second straight year, and rightfully so. How can you not feel that way after such a marquee win? Should they be printing the hats and T-shirts, however? That's a different discussion entirely.

While Chicago owns the inside track, the NFC North is far from being solidified. The Bears still have three division matchups on the docket over their final six games of the season. Outside of facing NFC North rivals, they'll also square off against the Jaguars and Bills. The only sure-fire victory is when they visit the Miami Dolphins in Week 14. With the margins still razor-thin, and the Bears currently 1-2 in the division, they are not on as solid ground as this latest win would suggest.

At the end of the day, the MVP is a quarterback's award. You may not like it, but that's the reality. Gibbs has been otherworldly this season and just put together a historic performance on Thanksgiving. He logged 21 carries for 205 yards, three touchdowns, and five receptions for 47 yards. Those are the second-most rushing yards on Thanksgiving in NFL history, and Gibbs tied Barry Sanders (1997) for the most rushing touchdowns on Thanksgiving by a Lions player in franchise history.

Gibbs has joined Eric Dickerson (1983) and Priest Holmes (2002) as the only players with at least 1,700 scrimmage yards and 18 total touchdowns in the first 11 games of a season in NFL history.

JAHMYR GIBBS 70-YARD TOUCHDOWN 🔥 pic.twitter.com/w7oihVzrsd

Again, these numbers are bonkers and will almost certainly give Gibbs the inside track at the Offensive Player of the Year award. Those who Jim Nantz pointed out were chanting "MVP" at Ford Field on Thursday, however, will be disappointed. That'll go to Joe Burrow, Brock Purdy, or whichever quarterback endears himself to the NFL at large.

He may deserve it, but the hardware Gibbs will be eyed for is OPOY and not MVP.

Jalen Hurts is the obvious top option at quarterback once he returns to full health. We're not talking about Hurts' standing as QB1 in Philadelphia. However, Howie Roseman has once again pulled a rabbit out of his hat. He plucked Joe Milton III off Dallas' practice squad, and you can't deny that what we've seen out of Milton doesn't warrant a longer look as a full-time starter in the NFL.

JOE MILTON AND DEVONTA SMITH DO IT AGAINPHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/TubiStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hjaMzRC3ub

It might not be with the Eagles, but you can't deny the raw ability that Milton possesses. The arm talent is obvious, and he was able to hang in against Dallas in a high-profile Thanksgiving matchup on the road in just his third career start.

The Eagles have done a fantastic job at parlaying assets into future draft capital. It's not out of the realm of possibility that they do the same with Milton -- who'll be a restricted free agent -- this offseason. For a team searching for a long-term starter at quarterback, why wouldn't you roll the dice on someone like Milton, who is 26 years old? He has far higher upside than Kirk Cousins, Geno Smith, Kyler Murray, and Daniel Jones, who'll also be free agents (albeit unrestricted) this offseason.

Nail, meet coffin. The Cowboys can put their playoff hopes to bed, unofficially. After blowing a 21-point lead to the Eagles on Thanksgiving, Dallas drops to 5-7 on the season. For the moment, they're in third place in the NFC East, and the path to the playoffs feels nonexistent, even if mathematically there's still a chance.

INTERCEPTED! EAGLES COMPLETE THE COMEBACK! pic.twitter.com/ymk4TF0H8K

They already are on the wrong side of the tiebreaker with the Giants after losing the season opener. They still have a Week 17 matchup to fully determine if that tiebreaker will be a factor. If not, it'll come down to division record, where New York has the advantage through Week 12 (2-1-1 vs. 2-2).

More dire for Dallas, the road ahead may make division and head-to-head tiebreakers moot. After falling to the Joe Milton-led Eagles, the Cowboys will now have to endure a three-game stretch of facing the Seahawks in Seattle, the Rams in Los Angeles (after the Week 14 bye), and then the Jacksonville Jaguars before they see the Giants. They'll, in all likelihood, be an underdog in all three of those games. If the oddsmakers are proved right, they're 5-10 before they kick off against the Giants.

After Thursday's showing, it's hard to have any confidence that they'll persevere and make a legitimate push to a division title.

It's not that Buffalo won't eventually land the No. 1 seed in the AFC, but it's hardly secure at this point even after a critical head-to-head win over Kansas City. The Bills are 10-1 on the season, which has them on the inside track for the first-round bye at the moment. However, the upcoming month does present some challenges. After heading up to New England to face a Drake Maye-less Patriots, Buffalo will face the Packers (road), Bears, and Broncos (road). That could result in some losses that open the door for some other contenders in the conference.

Specifically, that Broncos matchup in Denver looms large on Christmas Day as Sean Payton's team is currently the closest to Buffalo for the top spot in the conference. Again, the Bills are in a great position to be the No. 1 seed, but we've got a long way to go before locking in first-round bye plans.
